title: alpha-blended textures have invalid light level when SDFGI energy != 1.0
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.rc1.mono.official [481f36ed2] v4.6.dev5.mono.official [f5918a9d3] v4.0.stable.mono.official [92bee43ad] ### System information Godot v4.6.dev5.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7602) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300HF CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.91 GiB memory ### Issue description Because images can speak better than thousands of words (all these are assuming background energy 1.0): SDFGI energy 1.0 + sky contrib SDFGI energy 1.0 no sky contrib SDFGI energy 0.15 + sky contrib SDFGI energy 0.15 no sky contrib Alpha-blended textures are probably using background energy multiplier instead of SDFGI energy multiplier here; if background energy level is equalized with SDFGI energy level, the discrepancy between alpha-noalpha disappears. I understand that "Transparent materials are not present in the signed distance field generated by SDFGI.", and I'm not expecting them to contribute. I'd just expect energy levels to be treated in a consistent manner, because both SDFGI itself as well as `sdfgi_read_sky_light` setting is already affecting alpha-blended objects, but `sdfgi_energy` is not. Disabling SDFGI in any way obviously fixes the visual problem :) AFAIK, it's the amount of light that is added via sky contrib that highlights it (with non-bright skies this is not visible), and it _only_ affects materials with alpha. Sky diffuse lighting ignoring SDFGI energy for transparent materials is IMO the problem here. However, any hint on how to either work around this or just how to reduce the sky contribution without lowering the SDFGI energy level (without turning sky contribution off completely) would be appreciated as well - for ambient light, sky contrib is a float, but for SDFGI I could only find a binary 0-or-1 switch. PS. it's not limited to standard materials etc. Even a simple ``` void fragment() { vec4 tex = texture(albedo_texture, UV); ALBEDO = tex.rgb; ALPHA = 1.0; // note that commenting this out "fixes" the problem. } ``` triggers this, so it seems it's related to how SDFGI treats lighting stuff with alpha enabled. ### Steps to reproduce 1. have two materials/textures, one with alpha and one without, place them on two quads, and have a bright sky - with energy 1.0, everything looks fine though unpleasantly bright (pic 1), with energy 0.15 everything looks nice and reasonable (pic 2) 2. set SDFGI to e.g. 0.15 energy while keeping the rest on - notice that the quad with alpha is lit with amount of light ~equivalent to energy 1.0 (very bright), while the one without is 0.15 as expected (reasonably bright) (pic 3) 4. set energy to 1.0 but disable sky contribution. Everything is seemingly fine? (pic 4) 5. setting energy to > 1.0 also creates this artifact, but visually in reverse: alpha-blended texture still renders as with 1.0 energy (so it's darker then), while one without blending correctly increases the brightness. 6. if background energy level is equalized with SDFGI energy level, the discrepancy disappears (but obviously this makes the entire scene unacceptably dark) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Can be reproduced on the Godot Robot icon in an initial project, although it's harder to spot because the conditions are visually less extreme there. [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24672915/test.zip)
